definition: Deplore means to express strong disapproval of or sorrow about something.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word deplore. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know deplore should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Her toast began by deploring the whole tradition of toasts, then ran eleven affectionate minutes anyway.
Regret is private — a sigh over what happened, said to no one in particular — while deplore puts its sorrow and disapproval on the record, out loud.
Castigate goes further than deplore — deploring grieves over conduct from a distance; castigating hauls the guilty up by name and flays them for it.

To bemoan is to groan over something out loud — the weary, everyday complaint about traffic, prices, or paperwork. Deplore is graver and more formal: it declares strong disapproval or sorrow the way editorials and resolutions do. You bemoan an inconvenience; you deplore a wrong.

To lament is to grieve aloud — pure sorrow with no judgment attached. Deplore adds moral disapproval to the grief: it faults conduct even while it mourns. A demolished landmark is lamented; a cruel policy is deplored.

Complaining is smaller and wants a fix; deploring mourns aloud and on purpose, whether or not anything can still be done.
Deplore is disapproval in mourning dress — editorials, resolutions, and grandmothers use it about conduct and losses alike.
